AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a moderately attractive fundamental picture with a world-class franchise but meaningful near-term earnings-quality and valuation concerns. The franchise is exceptional: AWS reaccelerated to 28% YoY growth (fastest in 15 quarters) at 37.7% operating margins, advertising reached $70B+ TTM at high margins, and the platform flywheel continues to compound. Revenue growth is accelerating (QoQ +7.7% then +7.4%), operating cash flow surged to $35.52B/quarter, and the balance sheet is a fortress (D/E = 0.149, equity growing +20.9% in two quarters). However, operating margin compressed from 11.8% to 9.7% over two quarters, and Q3 net income ($21.19B) exceeded operating income ($17.42B) by $3.77B — indicating material below-the-line gains that are unlikely to recur, making the earnings beat lower quality. Valuation is mid-range at 34.65x PE (range 28.2–39.0x) with a 2.9% earnings yield versus 4.46% 10-year Treasury, offering limited margin of safety. The ~$200B 2026 capex plan compresses FCF to $11.2B TTM despite $139.5B OCF, creating genuine uncertainty about near-term returns. Near-term catalysts include Prime Day (June 23–26) and Q2 earnings (July 30) with strong guidance ($194–199B sales, $20–24B operating income), plus early Trainium external sales talks that could open a new revenue stream. These catalysts provide modest positive tilt but don't overcome the operating-margin compression and mid-range valuation. Score reflects a strong franchise with positive trajectory, tempered by earnings-quality questions and fair-to-slightly-rich valuation.
